# agent-spaces — Active Invariants

## acp.jobs.node-execution-ownership

Agent profiles may declare jobs.default_node and schedules may override it with execution.node. Each accepts one logical HRC node ID, a non-empty list, or the reserved all wildcard. Compilation emits canonical desiredJson.execution.nodes: concrete members are validated, deduplicated, and sorted; all remains exactly ["all"]; local and all mixed with concrete members are rejected. The owner set authorizes deliberate independent per-node fan-out in ACP and is never a source for a JobRun's singular execution identity. This contract is separate from HRC scope placement.

## agent-spaces.agent-harness-runtime-boundary

Praesidium has two supported execution lowerings from one ASP-owned semantic resolution boundary. The default agent-harness path constructs and operates a Pi AgentSessionRuntime through agent-harness-runtime. A custom Pi AgentSpacesResourceLoader is the sole direct-path resource-delivery boundary: it resolves ordered mutable and immutable-snapshot ASP sources, compiles the contextual prompt and reminder, and uses Pi's native loaders for selected resources without consuming an ASPC-produced frontier-harness plan, harness adapter lowering, generated merged Pi bundle, or generated external-harness home. The loader is created and reloaded inside Pi's replacement-session factory so new, resumed, forked, imported, and cwd-replaced sessions keep the same ASP resource authority. The direct runtime has three outer surfaces that all use the same createAgentHarnessRuntime factory: local foreground TUI/print execution selected by asp run, the HRC-operated headless agent-harness broker service, and an HRC-launched interactive TUI in a broker-leased tmux pane. The third surface is fresh and HRC-owned; it does not attach to a foreground session. Across its process boundary, broker-allocated turn identity and the broker's admitted session configuration bind before input delivery and session construction respectively. An inability to bind a proposed turn is a recoverable turn failure: the child returns a closed-code negative acknowledgement without closing the control channel or runtime, the driver delivers no pane input, and the broker preserves its normal accepted-input and idempotency boundary by opening and terminally failing the allocated turn before returning the invocation to ready. Session configuration failure remains fail-closed before construction; the child does not re-derive broker-owned auth or permission values. SDK-backed model configuration is independent of process hosting: agent-harness-tmux carries the SDK binding with pty/tmux execution rather than the in-process sentinel. The TUI starts with the loader-supplied praesidium-loader validation theme, while mechanical assertions and parity tests remain the correctness authority. Agents that explicitly select Claude Code or Codex CLI retain a compiler-backed compatibility path that may produce the artifacts those external harnesses require. Both lowerings consume shared ASP resolution semantics but own distinct post-resolution representations. The verifier-only agent-resource-parity/v1 format independently compares compiler output with the production direct resource loader for ASP-authored prompt mode/content, reminder presence/content, and effective skill catalog/package bytes across query, heartbeat, task, and maintenance for every valid fleet agent. HRC remains authority for runtime placement, lifecycle, session routing, supervision, and durable messaging; foreground asp run is a separate local session and does not attach to an existing HRC runtime. Broker-selected auth path, provider, mode, and composed environment bind the shared ModelRuntime before model lookup and session creation, without fallback to the foreground auth store. Every Earendil Pi object-sharing consumer—drivers/harness-pi-sdk, harness/harness-broker-pi-sdk, harness/agent-harness-runtime, harness/agent-harness, and spaces-integration-tests—resolves exact version 0.84.3 with coherent @earendil-works/pi-* lock entries. Runtime internal DTOs, credential transport beyond that binding, broker wire/process topology, and support for additional resource categories remain implementation choices unless another active contract fixes them.

## agent-spaces.agent-inspection-authority

Agent Spaces is the sole authority for canonical agent roster discovery and contextual inspection assembly. Its consumer-facing catalog and inspection operations accept only validated agent and project identifiers plus declared inspection overrides; filesystem paths, roots, environment snapshots, clocks, probe results, scaffolds, and compile options never cross that boundary. Agent Spaces resolves trusted project placement, current producer sources, and runtime context internally, validates a requested agent against that freshly resolved context, and returns only the shared public DTO. A project-neutral catalog never invents a project or emits project-contextual compile options, and lower-level context-taking primitives remain internal to the producer boundary for external consumers.

## agent-spaces.architecture-law

Active records under architecture/records are agent-spaces' durable architecture law. ADRs, generated projections, docs, tasks, chats, and comments are provenance unless an active record imports a predicate.

## agent-spaces.canonical-package-publication

Every staged ASP package manifest carries exactly {schema,repository,canonicalRemote,sourceCommit,setName,setVersion,builtAt} under praesidiumBuild. Canonical publication freshly fetches its named remote tracking ref, requires a clean source tree and sourceCommit containment by that fetched ref, preflights the coherent set against same-name/version replacement, and cache-empty fetches every published tarball while verifying its build tuple. Dev, force, skip-existing, and worktree publication paths are explicitly non-canonical and cannot emit canonical proof.

## agent-spaces.portable-immutable-source

A generated portable ASP lock records immutable space source authority only as repository identity plus canonical remote. Node-local mirror and store paths are explicit ASP-owned placement state and are never serialized into the lock. Immutable entries, including historical pins, resolve and populate snapshots from that canonical mirror placement; mutable @dev entries continue to resolve from the node-local agents root. Legacy path-bearing locks may be read only to regenerate them and are never repaired by rewriting path strings.

## agent-spaces.verify-gate

just verify is agent-spaces' local handoff gate and must include the architecture-records structure and projection-freshness check.
